title: Bernard Hilda's move to Paris; Herron Hill High School
summary: Back to his own schooling: Hilda's family returned to France, and Clarke went on to Herron Hill High School.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers

blocks.x: I've got to stop you. We've got to go back, because we got onto your brother but we left you at the age of 14 --
And this is important. We've got to find out how this happened. So all right, back you go.
Okay. Well, you see, I was going --
Oh, yeah, you met the friend, the fellow that's the agent here.
Yeah. Well, his people moved to Paris, you know, as soon as he finished secondary school.
His family moved to Paris, because I think his father became an ambassador or something. They were
French anyway, but his father married --
How do you spell that name, H-i-l-d-a?
I do think I've heard the name, yeah.
He's a very famous band leader.
So his father was an ambassador, was a French citizen, though, he had something to do with politics. And they went back -- his father moved back to France and took the family.
So how old was Bernard at that time, would you say?
Uh-huh. So then I went on to -- we were living in the same neighborhood. I went on to another school, something like in our neighborhood, but I had left secondary and went to high school.
Oh, I was just wondering if I'll hear another familiar name of Earl's, but I don't remember that one, no.
Well, Herron Hill High School and the Schenley High School, are the two famous schools.
Well, I think he did say that.
